caption: The drawing displays two distinct objects on a light beige, textured background. On the left side is a round, lidded box with a diameter of about six inches, depicted in brown and yellowish tones to represent the bark material, featuring etched decorations and a star-like geometric pattern on the top. The cylindrical sides are decorated with zigzag etching near the edges, and shadowing is drawn below and to the left, giving it three-dimensionality. On the right side is a single, curved object with a rectangular flat end and a hooked tip, colored in shades of brown to denote wood; it is labeled as having a length of six inches. The box and curved object are separately drawn and each is accompanied by handwritten notes in pencil at the lower left and right of the paper, respectively, identifying the origins (Penobscot Tribe, Eastern Woodland Hall), materials (bark for the box, wood for the implement), and brief descriptions of the objects. The sheet itself has a row of round perforations across the top edge, indicating it is from a spiral notebook.
title: Box and Basket Implement
